correctness.rationale: For all odd prime powers, the identity X^2=(c^2+ab)I proves X^[p]^k=(c^2+ab)^((p^k-1)/2)X. Each nonzero X=t^vY has unique primitive Y; smooth lifting of the nonzero quadratic cone produces exactly (q^2-1)q^(3r-h-2) primitive solutions at precision h. Splitting v at ceil(m/p^k) yields the full count. The explicit unit-plus-t example proves the maximal height, and the exact tail bound yields logarithmic concentration. Six small prime-field families are independently exhaustively checked by direct matrix multiplication with VERIFY_OK; finite checks are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Successive kernels of the restricted p-power map form a natural filtration of the nilpotent cone relevant to modular current Lie algebras. A complete all-length enumeration and an exact maximal height answer a more precise question than eventual nilpotence, and the logarithmic typical-height theorem describes a sharp statistical regime. The finite quadratic-lift count is an ingredient, not the sole claimed advance.
